card: Makes the default combined fee estimator in estimatesmartfee fall back to the block policy estimate whenever the mempool estimator cannot produce an estimate, rather than returning an error. It changes the mempool estimator to return an error instead of the minimum relay fee floor when the mempool lacks enough transaction data to fill block percentiles, preventing severe fee underestimation on nodes with empty or sparse mempools. Additionally, when mempool loading fails at startup, the estimator clears its mined-block window to prevent building estimates from stale state until new blocks arrive.
changed_since_previous: The core approach and behavior remain unchanged from the previous description.
evidence: PR description: 'Previously, case (ii) with a healthy mempool will returned the fee rate floor... This can be a significant underestimation, since the now-missing mempool may have held much higher-feerate transactions. The remaining cases surfaced the mempool error directly from the combined estimate.'

Commit ac0c630ebd: 'Flooring per call lets a later commit tell an unfilled percentile apart from a floored one, so it can return an error instead of the floor and let the combined estimate fall back to the block policy estimate.'
problem: When the mempool is sparse or empty (such as after a restart without persistence or when mempool.dat is missing or corrupt), the mempool fee estimator previously returned the fee floor, causing severe underestimation. In other states where the mempool estimator was unready (startup, low coverage, or during mempool loading), the combined estimator returned an error instead of falling back to usable block policy estimates.

risk.why: A bug in fee estimation logic could lead wallets or callers of estimatesmartfee to broadcast transactions with severely inaccurate fee rates, leading to stuck transactions or overpayment.

summary: Makes the default combined fee estimator (`estimatesmartfee` with `fee_rate_estimator=none`) fall back to the block policy estimate whenever the mempool estimator is unavailable or not ready, rather than surfacing an error. It also changes the mempool estimator to return an error when the mempool cannot fill block template percentiles instead of flooring to the minimum relay fee rate. Finally, it clears the mempool estimator's tracked mined-block stats when a mempool load fails at startup.
